## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The code change is correct. `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` is the only source of the `--timeout` default, and the updated `test_defaults` checks the new value. The one problem is that the user-facing README still states the old 30-second default.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/cli.py:3 — comments — This PR raises `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` to `60`, but `README.md:3` still says "Requests time out after 30 seconds unless you pass `--timeout SECONDS`." That line is now wrong for anyone who runs the CLI without `--timeout`. Could you change it to "60 seconds" in this PR? — Users reading the README will expect requests to give up after 30 seconds, while they actually wait up to 60 seconds before timing out.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `tests/test_cli.py:8` now asserts `args.timeout == 60` through `parse_args([])`, so it tests the new default as users see it. `test_explicit_options` (`tests/test_cli.py:14-15`) still checks that an explicit `--timeout 12` overrides the default, as the PR description says.
